#### What this PR does / why we need it:

It is a follow up of #125197, reducing populating of NodeToStatus map when possible. The structure of NodeToStatus is changed by introducing AbsentNodesStatus to pass the status message for absent nodes in the map.

Note: This PR breaks the interface of post filter plugins.  It's a second option to consider. In #125954 the solution proposed is not affecting the interface, but gives less flexibility.

issue_context.title: [scheduler] Improve Handling of Node Status
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

This issue is to track follow-ups from #125197, which addressed a performance issue related to the NodeToStatusMap. There are latent issues which we would like to address to prevent future regressions. We can either improve NodeToStatusMap to support some of the below operations more efficiently, or come up with different way to propagate these statuses through the scheduler.

current problems:
- we loop through all nodes to set the [same status](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae37c21645c0fc04bbb0202ad1eba6ba4438d23/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L458-L462)
  - w/ current implementation, only need to set Unschedulable status - see [comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125197#discussion_r1621723775)
- we [loop through all nodes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae37c21645c0fc04bbb0202ad1eba6ba4438d23/pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go#L419-L430) when determining preemption candidates, so that we can create an [error message](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dae37c21645c0fc04bbb0202ad1eba6ba4438d23/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L392-L397) based on the UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status. this error message can be generated more efficiently. also see [comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125197/files#r1621778045)

other considerations:
- when operating over many nodes, hashing node name string is hotspot when doing hashmap gets/sets. consider creating a lightweight `NodeKey` type, which, for a scheduling cycle, references an existing node. This type should be cheap to hash  (+allow lookup in [flat data structure](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a2911e06a7cd393f7cce088b8399f889527b517f/pkg/scheduler/internal/cache/snapshot.go#L33)), and is safer than string node name, as it is guaranteed to reference a valid node.
- consider updating scheduler to not call postfilter plugins when all nodes are `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`. at least, we should  reconcile the documented behavior [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a2911e06a7cd393f7cce088b8399f889527b517f/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L454-L456) and [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a2911e06a7cd393f7cce088b8399f889527b517f/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L90) and [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a2911e06a7cd393f7cce088b8399f889527b517f/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L97-L98)
- consider changing [Status](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a2911e06a7cd393f7cce088b8399f889527b517f/pkg/scheduler/framework/interface.go#L181) to an immutable type, so it can be safely shared.

/sig scheduling

### Why is this needed?

The current implementation includes some operations which may cause future performance regression. Additionally, there is some room for simplification.

> consider updating scheduler to not call postfilter plugins when all nodes are UnschedulableAndUnresolvable. 

I personally prefer this approach. This seems to be sufficient and the changes are relatively small.

> consider updating scheduler to not call postfilter plugins when all nodes are UnschedulableAndUnresolvable.

We cannot take this way, UnschedulableAndUnresolvable has the meaning only to plugin(s) that do preemption-ish stuff. 
But, there are some other usecases in PostFilter, such as record something, clean up something, etc when each scheduling fails.

> We cannot take this way, UnschedulableAndUnresolvable has the meaning only to plugin(s) that do preemption-ish stuff.
But, there are some other usecases in PostFilter, such as record something, clean up something, etc when each scheduling fails.

Ah right. We have already changed current behaviour to not set `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` for allNodes if preFilter fails, not sure if this will break some custom postFilter plugins.
Then I think instead of `not call postfilter`, passing an empty NodeToStatus map may be enough. However, we'll need a new field in NodeToStatus map  to indicate that all nodes are `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` for plugins.

> We cannot take this way, UnschedulableAndUnresolvable has the meaning only to plugin(s) that do preemption-ish stuff.

Still, the preemption plugin could exit early if can tell that all nodes where UnschedulableAndUnresolvable
@YamasouA this is not a task that is friendly to newcomers. Do you have experience writing code for the scheduler? Or perhaps you have someone that can mentor you already?
No worries Aldo, I'm with them.

I have been experimenting with these improvements over the past two weeks (#125954). Unfortunately, I forgot to assign myself to the issue, my bad. Nevertheless, the PR addresses only the "current problems" part of the improvements. I think the lightweight `NodeKey` and immutable `Status` types are still worth exploring, but in my opinion both would require changes in plugins' interface.

review_comments: Do we need to worry about the case where multiple plugins set this to different values in the same scheduling cycle? If so, we may consider the absent node status to either stay the same, or become progressively less schedulable - `Unschedulable` to `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` is fine, but not the reverse

Only post filter plugins use `NodeToStatus` (receive it as an argument), but as I understand, they treat it as a read-only data structure. It means that `absentNodesStatus` shouldn't be overwritten in any place.

@sanposhiho @alculquicondor Am I right that the post filter plugins shouldn't modify the `NodeToStatus` map?

`NodeToStatus` should be read-only in PostFilter from my memory, yes. 
But, this PR actually uses `SetAbsentNodesStatus` in preemption.go, right? Could other postfilter plugins want to do the same?

`preemption.go` creates new NodeToStatus, but treats the PostFilter's arg as read-only. I think, to emphasize the desired way, we could create an interface with read-only methods and pass it to post filter plugins. Then, they would be able to create their own new maps (by instantiating NodeToStatus directly), but not break the current one (because of the interface).

```go
type NodeToStatusReader interface {
    Get(nodeName string) *Status
    Len() int
    AbsentNodesStatus() *Status
    ForEach(fn func(nodeName string, status *Status))
}
```

We could even name the interface `NodeToStatusMap` not to break the post filter plugins that doesn't use the map at all.
Created `NodeToStatusReader` interface and `NodeToStatusMap` as its alias (not to break all the plugins as described above)

Got it regarding  `SetAbsentNodesStatus` in preemption.go (Sorry I didn't read through the PR very well).

Regarding `NodeToStatusReader`, I know if we had come up with the idea at day 1, it'd have been a better idea to emphasize it's read-only though, 
to introduce this change now looks so big that the merit (emphasize it's read-only) doesn't overcome the demerit (an effort would be required for all existing custom preemption developers).
So, I'm -1 for it. Maybe we just mention it's read-only somewhere around PostFilter interface for clarification.

I think that passing the `NodeToStatusReader` interface (aliased as `NodeToStatusMap`) won't break more plugins than solution without the interface (i.e. passing the `NodeToStatus` struct directly). 

Plugins that doesn't read the map or those that only pass it e.g. to the `Preempt` method, won't break, because the type name `framework.NodeToStatusMap` will match the previous one. 

The only plugins that will require attention are those that read the map, but passing the struct directly will force the same, since all operations on map are hidden under the methods.

> Then, another angle though, how about just adding a status to PostFilter interface, rather than managing it in NodeToStatusMap in the first place?

I'm not sure if this will give us any noticeable advantage. It would still require the same changes as in this PR, except modification of the map. By managing the absent status in `NodeToStatus` as proposed in this PR, it could be more straightforward to use, as both map and absent status are coupled naturally. Especially, absent status won't be accidentally ignored in the future, which could happen if handled separately. 

Your proposal would also break more PostFilter plugins, as the new arg would need to be added for each of them. In this PR `dynamicresources` plugin could not be changed at all, but did this to use the more preferable interface name over the alias.

We could even try to optimize the `NodeToStatus` in the future, by tracking changes of statuses and stating explicitly if all the nodes are `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`, even if the map is non-empty (e.g. when filter plugins mark all the nodes as `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`).

Yeah, I meant, it's a wider blast radius but smaller change (my proposal) vs a narrower blast radius but bigger change (yours), and I preferr **_ed_** mine a lot more, from that perspective.

> Especially, absent status won't be accidentally ignored in the future, which could happen if handled separately.

But, this is a critical point. Mine would require people to be aware of a new `filterStatus` for a correct preemption, which we can easily imagine people miss it.

Okay, I'm now convinced. Let's go with the current `Reader` interface design.
@macsko Please update a release note.
Updated

Given all `NewNodeToStatus` is called with `absentNodesStatus=UnschedulableAndUnresolvable`,
1. Can we remove `absentNodesStatus` from `NewNodeToStatus`? 
2. Can we remove `NewDefaultNodeToStatus` and use `NewNodeToStatus` with nil map instead?

Not for all cases `NewNodeToStatus` is called with the same status. All codes are `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` for sure, but the `reasons` differ depending on the usage. I think removing `absentNodesStatus` arg from `NewNodeToStatus` doesn't give us that much advantage.
please add a unit test for the function.
Added
Moved fetching all nodes to the branch where `absentNodesStatus` is matching given code, so altered the comment differently.
Love it now!

this method is only used once. is it worth adding it to the interface, versus just defining it as a function in preemption.go? i.e. do we have good reason to believe plugin developers will use this method?

We want to hide `absentNodesStatus` in `NodeToStatusReader` to reduce the risks of not handling this field (see [comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126022#discussion_r1683123490)). If we move contents of this method back to the preemption.go, we would need to expose `AbsentNodesStatus()` and `ForEachExplicitNode()` in the interface, what we don't want to do.
Ack. Thanks for the explaination.
